places.name: Netherfield
places.note: A large house in Hertfordshire, let at last. Austen invented it; placed here near Hertford, about three miles from Longbourn.

places.name: Longbourn
places.note: The Bennets' home village in Hertfordshire, a mile from Meryton. Invented by Austen; placed near Hertford.

places.name: Meryton
places.note: The market town near Longbourn. Austen invented it; it is often taken to be modelled on Hertford, so it sits there.

places.name: Lucas Lodge
places.note: Sir William Lucas's house, about a mile from Meryton (invented; placed near Hertford).

places.name: Hertfordshire
places.note: The county north of London where the Bennets live.

places.name: London
places.note: Town: half a day's drive south of Meryton.

places.name: St. James's
places.note: The royal court at St James's Palace, London, where gentlemen were presented to the King.

places.name: Cheapside
places.note: A busy trading street in the City of London: a merchant's address, not a fashionable one.

places.name: Grosvenor Street
places.note: A fashionable street in Mayfair, London, where Mr Hurst has a house.

places.name: Gracechurch Street
places.note: A street in the City of London, near the merchants' quarter, where the Gardiners live.

places.name: Derbyshire
places.note: A county of hills and dales in the north Midlands.

places.name: Pemberley
places.note: A great estate in Derbyshire. Austen invented it; it is often linked with Chatsworth, so it is placed there.

places.name: Lambton
places.note: A small Derbyshire market town near Pemberley. Invented; placed at Bakewell, its usual identification.

places.name: Kent
places.note: The county south-east of London.

places.name: Hunsford
places.note: A parish in Kent near Westerham, where Mr Collins has his living. Invented; placed at Westerham.

places.name: Rosings
places.note: Lady Catherine de Bourgh's great house in Kent, near Hunsford. Invented; placed near Chevening.

places.name: Bromley
places.note: A posting town on the road between London and Kent, where travellers change horses.

places.name: Brighton
places.note: The fashionable seaside resort on the Sussex coast.

places.name: Bath
places.note: The spa city in Somerset, a resort of fashionable society.

places.name: Ramsgate
places.note: A seaside town on the Kent coast.

places.name: Cambridge
places.note: The university town.

places.name: the Lakes
places.note: The Lake District in the north-west of England, a favourite tour for its mountains and lakes.

places.name: Oxford
places.note: The university city, on the road north from London.

places.name: Blenheim
places.note: Blenheim Palace near Woodstock, the Duke of Marlborough's seat, a sight for travellers.

places.name: Warwick
places.note: A county town with a famous castle, on the tourists' road north.

places.name: Kenelworth
places.note: Kenilworth, Warwickshire, with its ruined castle.

places.name: Birmingham
places.note: The busy manufacturing town in the Midlands.

places.name: Matlock
places.note: A Derbyshire spa among celebrated scenery.

places.name: Chatsworth
places.note: Chatsworth House, the Duke of Devonshire's seat in Derbyshire.

places.name: Dovedale
places.note: A limestone valley in the Peak, famous for its scenery.

places.name: Newcastle
places.note: Newcastle upon Tyne, far in the North of England.

places.name: Scotland
places.note: North of the border, where marriage laws were looser than England's.

places.name: Gretna Green
places.note: The first village over the Scottish border, where couples could marry without banns or consent.

places.name: Epsom
places.note: A Surrey town on the road between Brighton and London.

places.name: Clapham
places.note: Then a village just south of London, on the Brighton road.

places.name: Barnet
places.note: A coaching town on the Great North Road out of London.

places.name: Hatfield
places.note: A Hertfordshire coaching town on the Great North Road.
